summary.name: AirPoise
summary.one_liner: A free macOS menu-bar app that uses AirPods motion sensors to coach posture and trigger actions from head gestures.
use_cases: Reminding yourself to sit upright during desk work
Triggering Mac shortcuts or scripts with head nods
Tracking time spent in good posture each day
Controlling play/pause or Spaces without using hands
summary.what_it_does: AirPoise reads head pose from AirPods motion data (CMDeviceMotion) and compares it to a calibrated upright position, measuring chin-forward flexion and ear-to-shoulder side tilt. When a bad pose is held too long, it shows a glass overlay with an optional ping or spoken cue. It also recognizes sixteen head gestures (an excursion that returns) that can be bound to keystrokes, Shortcuts actions, URLs, scripts, media keys, and other Mac functions. The page says it keeps a daily time-in-band score, and that settings are adjustable via sliders, with a walk-rejection filter and per-axis invert. It does not use a camera or network, and it cannot detect spinal posture, which the page states openly.
notable: Uses AirPods IMU via CoreMotion with no camera, cloud, or analytics
Sixteen configurable head gestures bindable to keystrokes, Shortcuts, scripts and more
Gravity-referenced calibration; the page admits it cannot judge spinal posture
Listed as open source on GitHub (jaskirat1616/AirPoise) in awesome-mac lists
caveats: Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later; Intel Macs on Sonoma may run but are not confirmed
Only works with supported AirPods models with head tracking
Cannot detect a rounded back: a level head on a slouched spine still reads as good posture
Windows is not supported because CoreMotion is Apple-only
Daily score, custom bindings, and sound/spoken cues are listed as upcoming (v1.1, v1.2, soon)
